title: Adaptive Deadline Packer for Streaming Chat: KV-aware GPU Fit Heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: implement a production-ready batch-formation heuristic for streaming chat that reduces tail latency variance while maximizing GPU utilization and minimizing KV cache thrash. The packer should operate on an ongoing queue of streaming requests and form micro-batches using a soft-deadline arbitration approach combined with KV-slot affinity and a GPU-fit estimator. This is intended for hosted and dedicated modes and will be feature-flagged for Canary rollout.
background_and_problem_statement: Current continuous-batching policies either prioritize throughput (packing until GPU slab full) or strict latency (serve immediately), which causes either high 95th/99th latency or wasted GPU cycles and KV eviction storms. Streaming chat adds extra constraints: partially-completed responses keep KV state active, and variable token budgets mean batch size alone is a poor proxy for memory impact. We need a heuristic that reasons about per-request deadlines, estimated KV footprint, and fragmentation-aware GPU fitting to avoid preemptive OOMs and frequent KV compaction that spikes latency.
proposed_approach: Maintain a sliding pending-window (configurable, default 40ms) of incoming streaming chat turns.
Every pack cycle compute an affinity score for each pending request: score = w_deadline*urgency + w_locality*kv_affinity + w_session*session_coalesce - w_memory*estimated_gpu_cost.
Urgency = soft deadline remaining; deadlines derive from request-level latency SLO and turn-specific min_response_time hints from SDK.
KV affinity = probability that request will access the same KV slots as the in-flight batch (calculated from recent session token hashes + conversation history fingerprint).
Estimated GPU cost uses a microbench model: base_model_cost + per_token_factor*expected_new_tokens + kv_slot_penalty*(#new_slots) + slab_fragmentation_multiplier.
Pack greedily by descending score until the next item would push estimated_gpu_cost over the heuristic GPU slab target OR would violate a hard latency cutoff (configurable).
If memory pressure is high, trigger one of fallback actions: reduce max batch size, compress KV (lossy compression profile), or route lower-priority requests to a quantized model variant.

Continuously recalibrate weights (w_*) online using reservoir sampling of observed latencies and eviction outcomes; maintain a small RL-lite tuner that nudges coefficients to meet 95th latency and eviction-rate targets.
Expose telemetry for chosen score components per batch to the Console for drill-down and for automated regression alerts in Optimize.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Soft-deadline window increases average latency slightly for low-priority requests but reduces 99th latency spikes by avoiding KV churn.
Affinity heuristics reduce KV duplication but add CPU work to score computation; CPU is cheap relative to GPU cost but we must guard against hot paths in the grpc/edge workers.
Estimating GPU cost requires a compact predictive model kept in-sync with runtime kernel selection changes; mismatch can cause underpacking or OOM risk—hence canary + simulation before rollouts.
Online tuning adds complexity but avoids manual recalibration across varying traffic shapes. We'll limit actuator range and add safe-guards (never exceed configured hard limits).
metrics_and_success_criteria: Primary: 95th latency for streaming chat tokens decreases by >=10% relative to baseline under target load profile, without increasing mean cost-per-token by more than 3%.
Secondary: KV eviction rate decreases by >=20% during steady-state conversational workloads.
Safety: no increase in OOM incidents on canary hosts; fragmentation ratio (wasted_slab_bytes/total_slab_bytes) reduced or stable.
Operational: feature flag kill-switch under 30s, and rollout can be throttled by region and customer tier.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests covering score computation edge cases (empty history, max_slots, extreme token budgets).
Simulated loadbench with replayed production conversation traces demonstrating metric targets in metrics_and_success_criteria.
Canary A/B at 10% production traffic for 48 hours with no regression on P99 latency or increased OOMs.
Documentation of runtime knobs and a Console dashboard showing per-batch score breakdown.
rollout_plan: Merge prototype behind feature flag (PR link in attachments).
Internal loadbench and chaos tests vs current batcher; tune weights offline until staging targets met.
Canary: 10% of new streaming sessions across non-critical regions for 48h. Monitor alerts (p99 latency, OOM, KV evictions).
Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with step ramp of 2x traffic every 24h if metrics pass.
implementation_notes: Implement core scoring in C++ hot path with a thin Go wrapper for config; avoid Python on the hot path to maintain latency budgets.
Leverage existing KV fingerprinting utility from ENG-54011 to compute slot-affinity cheaply.
GPU cost predictor will be a small lookup table plus linear terms updated from nightly microbench jobs. Keep compatibility hooks for kernel selection changes.
progress: 2026-03-12: Spike complete. Prototype scoring function implemented in a test harness (single-host). Early microbench shows 12% reduction in 95th latency in low-traffic sims.
2026-03-13: Integrated KV fingerprinting (reuse code from ENG-54011). Found edge-case: long-running sessions with many short turns increase #new_slots; added a decay factor to slot penalty.
2026-03-14: Implemented GPU cost estimator and safety cutoff. Preparing PR for code review and staging run. Config knobs added to Console for canaries.
